What are y'all's thoughts on red dot and holographic sights, specifically for AR-15 builds but for more general use as well?

I've recently been making a few changes to a stock Stag 1L I've had but not really used for a few years - new magpul stock, grip, etc, as well as some new optics. Someone gave me a Chinese POS red dot that was turning off and on every other shot, so I just decided to bite the bullet and got an Aimpoint Patrol Rifle Optic (PRO) in a LaRue mount (so I can co-witness mbus rear sight with A2 front sight through lower 1/3).

I've only been able to get out and shoot it once so far, to get it sighted in and do a little plinking, but so far I'm loving the PRO.

I'm interested to hear others' experiences, though. I've heard good things about Vortex as a more budget-friendly option; interested in pros/cons of Eotech vs Aimpoint; etc, etc. So what do y'all use and how's it holding up?

A quality red dot (ie Aimpoint) is the way to go for a general purpose carbine. Having used one in combat imo it's the only way to go (disregarding special purposes like DMR/SPR which should run a 1-4x or 1-8x optic)

Right, I'm really liking my aimpoint pro so far.

Any experience with something like Vortex? Trying to convince a friend to get something better than chinese POS for his; looking at the SPARC or Strikefire because the Aimpoint is kind of a hard sell with the price.

Also have a .308 build that needs optics; any recommendations on a 1-4x? DSG has trijicon accupoint 1-4x24 sights for around $875 right now, with an American Defense mount included... seems to be basically regular price but with a free $150 mount. But I don't know that I quite want to jump into it that much yet.

I had a vortex and it's OK for light duty/non serious work, but I'd never run one on a weapon I was going to depend on for work (.mil/police/contract work) it's just not in the same tier as an Aimpoint.

The way I look at gun stuff, if you could see using that weapon in a situation where your life depends on it it's worth the extra $ for quality, if it's just a range toy ok cool buy w/e.

Magnified optics there's a much wider range of good choices than red dots, where it's pretty much just Aimpoint (I'm not an eotech fan, low battery life and relatively fragile among other issues). With 1-4x a lot more of it is going to be personal preference, especially in retical selection. The trijicon is def a solid choice I know a few dudes with them who are very satisfied. As for the American Defense mount, I'm not a huge fan of them I'd much rather run a LaRue Tactical mount.

Yeah, I've got a LaRue mount for my aimpoint and folding rear/fixed front irons co-witnessed through the lower third. Initial impressions are good, but the real test will be how well it holds up over time.

Any particular issues with American Defense?
The're ok, I just always felt the larue stuff was better, that and I can say from personal experience that an aimpoint in a LRT mount will hold zero through pretty much anything.
I have a Vortex SPARC II AND VMX-3T magnifier and LOVE them. Excellent product at a good price from an outstanding company with a bulletproof warranty

having a vortex instead of a top shelf optic, you'll be just fine.

I use a EOTech 512 with a flip-in Sightmark 4x magnifier. It's great. I wouldn't bother spending too much money on the magnifier (the EO Tech magnifier is too damn expensive/overpriced.) Usually you want to pay good money for glass, but that's in a scope. A magnifier doesn't have anything to do with your aimpoint or accuracy (that's all in the reddot), and the mount doesn't have to be repeatable, so go for the <$100 option.
Aimpoint for sure. They are practically indestructible. Just look up aimpoint torture test and you'll see what I'm talking about.

I run a Vortex SPARC II and VMX-3T magnifier on my Colt LE6720R Talo Edition. I absolutely love it. Vortex makes a great product at a good price point and stands behind their warranty better than any company I've ever dealt with

I've got an EoTech with GGG flip-up dust covers and I love the thing. There is a reason why EoTech and Aimpoint have back-and-forth debates online like 9mm vs. .40 S&W--They're both great options and people have their preference between the two. Between EoTech and Aimpoint, one is not better than the other and which one you like best is really going to be a personal decision.
I've always been a fan of Eotech's reticle and the fact that it's easy to use with both eyes open.

I've had opportunities to play with optics that I would have never personally purchased, and although I see the appeal, they are not a go-to for me. It all comes down to what you are accustomed to, and for me, that's the good ol' iron sights. From some of the higher end red dots, like C-More and Aimpoint, to the cheap knockoffs a la BSA and UTG, nothing has made me more comfortable than some old buckhorn style sights or a peep. Giving credit where it's due, I have a much easier time acquiring a target at night with a red dot, than I do iron sights.

Bottom line, it's just what you're used to, and my sights never need to have a battery change.

I feel its better to not use a red dot or holo sight at all, and to organically become skilled at aiming because in a life or death situation you need to be able to instinctively and reflexively shoot without any hesitation. The extra second it takes to use the red dot/holo could be the death of you.

What a strange situation. Part of me thinks that football players (in general but especially in the BPL) are spoon fed too much. As the article says it is the individuals responsibility to make sure their visas are all in order - this is surely the case for 90% of foreigners working in England - but not if you're a football player.

The club sort out your living situation, language classes, school for your kids, your internet provider, wash your undies but then again, why not? The club have just invested a significant amount of money on 'purchasing' you and are shelling out a decent wage so why not make life as easy as possible so you can play better as in the end, you're just another investment for the club/business to try and improve and make more money. The club have put themselves in this position and a small error has made them look very, very silly indeed.

I still believe players should be made to take more responsibility but in this scenario I think QPR have screwed up proper - much like their transfer business over the last few years. £50,000 a week? In a promoted side? That's crazy!
